ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features

s1.syndrome_frame: Crusty skin lesion with irregular shape and multiple superficial crusts in the fronto-orbital region, present for several months, with evidence of invasion into the reticular dermis
salient_findings: Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Marked regression of the plaque after treatment, but with residual papular lesions
key_facts: 59-year-old man
Crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
No significant past medical history
Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Treatment with cemiplimab 350 mg every 3 weeks
Marked regression of the plaque after five cycles of treatment
Residual papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma on dermoscopic evaluation
Decreased uptake in the original lesion on follow-up PET/CT

shortlist.label: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial biopsy diagnosis and primary treatment target

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopic evaluation of residual papules showed features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Basosquamous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to mixed features of squamous and basal cell carcinomas in the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis suggest potential for sarcomatoid differentiation

shortlist.label: Adenosquamous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Given the complex presentation and potential for dual differentiation in skin cancers

raw.rationale: The presence of both squamous cell carcinoma features on biopsy and residual papular lesions with features typical of basal cell carcinoma after treatment suggests a diagnosis that encompasses both types of skin cancer, which is most consistent with basosquamous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Does not fully explain the basal cell carcinoma features in the residual papules

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Does not account for the initial biopsy findings consistent with squamous cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features
rejected.why: There is no mention of sarcomatoid features in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Adenosquamous carcinoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is not supported by the clinical or pathological findings presented
